_readme: Slot table: our own description of what each pre-recorded motion does.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: slot internals cannot be read back from the robot.
'phorce list' tells you a slot's id and name and nothing else -- not its
direction, not its size, not the pose it starts from. So we describe them
here, and the decider picks a slot by matching this description.
LAYOUT: a 3x3 grid (3 directions x 3 amplitudes) in slots 1-9, plus slot 10,
the settle/rest motion. Slots 1-50 exist on the robot; we use 10.
THE POSES ARE PLACEHOLDERS -- every slot below has "placeholder": true and
the decider logs a warning at startup while any remain. Fill them in after
teaching the motions in phorce Studio:
1. Teach the motion (servo off, move by hand, record, save to the slot).
2. Read the joint angles at the START of the recording -> start_pose.
3. Read the joint angles at the END of the recording  -> end_pose.
('phorce-console' shows live axis positions; axis[i].pos.)
4. Paste them here in radians, in the order given by "axes", and delete
that slot's "placeholder" flag.
start_pose is what matters most: the decider prefers the slot whose start
pose is closest to where the robot actually is, so transitions stay smooth.
ADDING MORE SLOTS: any number of slots may share a (direction, amplitude)
cell. When several match, the pose score picks between them -- so teaching
two variants of 'left/large' from different rest postures is useful, not a
conflict.
"axes" lists which of the robot's 12 axes we use, and fixes the order of
every start_pose / end_pose array in this file.

3.desc: left, large sway (answers strong stirring on the left)

6.desc: center, large rock (answers strong stirring, centered)

9.desc: right, large sway (answers strong stirring on the right)

10.desc: settle / soothe-down to rest -- the last step of the wind-down ramp
